headline: PM Tareque Rahman inaugurates July Uprising Memorial Museum
summary: The new museum aims to preserve the history of the July Uprising, opening to the general public on Thursday, August 6. It features various galleries and historical artifacts.
details: Prime Minister Tareque Rahman inaugurated the July Gono Obbhutthan Smriti Jadughar (July Uprising Memorial Museum) on Wednesday, August 5, at 9 AM. He unveiled the plaque as the chief guest.
Following the inauguration, the Prime Minister toured various galleries, preserved artifacts, photographs, documents, and memorabilia within the museum.
On the opening day, the museum was reserved for special guests and members of the July martyr families. It will open to the general public from Thursday, August 6.
Online ticket collection will be available for visitors. Tickets are priced at BDT 50 for adult visitors and BDT 25 for children.
Former Chief Adviser of the interim government, Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus, was present with the Prime Minister. Other advisors and cabinet members also attended the event.
caption:
Bangladesh's history now has a new home. The July Uprising Memorial Museum has been officially inaugurated by Prime Minister Tareque Rahman.

Prime Minister Tareque Rahman inaugurated the July Gono Obbhutthan Smriti Jadughar (July Uprising Memorial Museum) on Wednesday, August 5, at 9 AM. He unveiled the plaque as the chief guest.

Following the inauguration, the Prime Minister toured various galleries, preserved artifacts, photographs, documents, and memorabilia within the museum.

On the opening day, the museum was reserved for special guests and members of the July martyr families. It will open to the general public from Thursday, August 6.

Online ticket collection will be available for visitors. Tickets are priced at BDT 50 for adult visitors and BDT 25 for children.

Former Chief Adviser of the interim government, Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus, was present with the Prime Minister. Other advisors and cabinet members also attended the event.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News

headline_marked: Digital forensics uncovers [[Sheikh Hasina's secret telecom network]] during escape
headline: Digital forensics uncovers Sheikh Hasina's secret telecom network during escape
summary: A digital forensic team has revealed details of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's secret communication network, including the use of fake NID-registered numbers and satellite phones, during the internet blackout in July-August 2024.
details: The International Criminal Tribunal's Digital Forensic Team has unveiled Sheikh Hasina's secret telecom network and startling information about her escape. This network utilized hidden numbers obtained with fake national identity cards and satellite phones for all her final communications during the nationwide internet shutdown in July-August 2024.

During the July 2024 uprising, an unprecedented internet blackout was imposed across Bangladesh to suppress the movement. While digital communication channels were shut down, high-speed internet remained active at Ganabhaban, the Prime Minister's residence.

This was facilitated by a special backup system of the Bangabandhu Satellite (now Bangladesh Satellite), with a tower dump installed on the Ganabhaban roof. Digital forensic expert Tanvir Hasan Zoha confirmed that despite the nationwide shutdown, Ganabhaban maintained internet connectivity through the Bangabandhu Satellite, configured for high-speed use.

The ousted former Prime Minister reportedly understood the gravity of the situation by August 1. Following a one-point declaration on August 3, her phone was used to contact at least 70 numbers, 11 of which were registered with names and photos but belonged to non-existent individuals.

By August 4, Sheikh Hasina became concerned about the security of her personal phone number. She then opted for satellite phones and personal numbers of Ganabhaban staff for communication, directly contacting Indian Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar via satellite phone to seek temporary asylum.

After receiving a green light from Delhi, a swift escape plan was initiated. Sheikh Hasina and her sister, Sheikh Rehana, were transported by an Air Force MI-17 helicopter to Kurmitola's Air Movement area.

During 20 minutes spent in the VIP room there, she made two phone calls. One was to a number registered in her daughter Putul's name abroad, but the number was active within Bangladesh. The other call was made just one minute before takeoff.
Sources indicate that Sheikh Hasina began sending secret text messages to relatives about leaving the country from August 1, though forensic analysis of all SMS messages is still ongoing.

All communication data belonging to Sheikh Hasina was allegedly erased by former army official Ziaul Ahsan, who has been arrested in a disappearance case. He reportedly established a private server system at his residence in Jalsiri.

Tanvir Hasan Zoha stated that Ziaul Ahsan's building lacked normal electricity supply, yet he forcibly secured more power than usual. This suggests he created his own 'digital mirror house' there to manage and potentially hide data.
